newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian guerrilla attacks leave at least 14 dead.
newsitem.headline: Colombian guerrilla attacks leave at least 14 dead.

text.p: At least 14 soldiers and policemen were killed in clashes with leftist rebels in central and southern Colombia on Friday, officials and military sources said.

They said the worst fighting occurred in a rural area of southeastern Guaviare province where 10 to 15 soldiers were killed in an apparent ambush by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas.
Guaviare Gov. Juan Carlos Medina confirmed the attack in a remote part of the jungle-covered province known as La Carpa, about three hours by riverboat from the provincial capital.
He told the RCN radio network that there were unconfirmed reports that as many as 15 soldiers had been killed and an equal number wounded in the fighting.

Officials said four policemen were killed late on Friday in fighting with suspected FARC rebels manning a makeshift roadblock in the municipality of San Cayetano, about 30 miles (50 km) north of Bogota in central Cundinamarca province.
Guerrillas launched a nationwide offensive last weekend in which dozens of police and government troops were killed in some of the worst fighting Colombia has seen in recent years.

The FARC, Colombia's largest rebel group, grew out of peasant militias founded in 1948. It was officially founded as a Marxist, pro-Soviet group in 1964 and has been fighting for more than three decades to topple the Colombian government.
